subtitle: A princess of grief carves a house for Vishnu amidst Shiva’s city of stone

panels.shot: sweeping low-angle wide of Chandrika Devi before the half-built Ananta Vasudeva temple, stone blocks and scaffold rising against the Bhubaneswar skyline of spires
panels.action: Chandrika Devi stands in regal but simple widow’s garments, hand resting on a carved block with Vishnu motifs, as Shaiva temple towers of Bhubaneswar loom in the hazy distance and her own shrine’s shikhara rises in fresh stone.

dialogue.text: In 13th-century Bhubaneswar, where Shiva’s spires ruled the skyline, a widowed Ganga princess named Chandrika Devi dared to raise a great house for Vishnu—carving her own legacy into stone.

i18n.hi: तेरहवीं सदी के भुवनेश्वर में, जहाँ शिव के शिखरों ने आसमान थाम रखा था, गंगा की विधवा राजकुमारी चन्द्रिका देवी ने विष्णु का विराट घर उठाने की हिम्मत की—अपनी विरासत पत्थर में लिख दी।

panels.shot: bird’s-eye over Bhubaneswar’s dense forest of medieval temple towers and the Bindusagar tank, morning light catching on stone
panels.action: A panoramic view of early 13th-century Bhubaneswar shows clustered Shaiva temples with curving Rekha deuls and the broad Bindusagar tank, priests and townsfolk moving along stone ghats.

dialogue.text: Bhubaneswar was already old—a city of Shiva, its land crowded with linga shrines and curving towers, its ponds ringed by priests and pilgrims who whispered mantras into the water.

i18n.hi: भुवनेश्वर तब भी पुराना था—शिव का शहर, भूमि लिंग मंदिरों और मुड़ी हुई मीनारों से भरी, तालाबों के घेरे में पुरोहित और यात्री जो पानी पर मंत्र फुसफुसाते थे।

panels.shot: slow push-in on a weathered stone inscription slab lying in a British-style museum case
panels.action: A stone slab bearing medieval Odia-Nagari script lies under glass in a modern museum case, lit from above, its incised letters sharp and orderly.

dialogue.text: Centuries later, a single stone record—the Ananta Vasudeva inscription now in the British Museum—would speak her name and deed, preserving what the city’s daily gossip forgot.

i18n.hi: सदियों बाद, एक अकेली पत्थर की ताम्रपट्ट—अनन्त वासुदेव की अभिलेख, जो अब ब्रिटिश संग्रहालय में है—उसका नाम और काम सुनाएगी, जो शहर की रोज़ की बातों से छूट गया था।

panels.shot: intimate interior mid-shot in a royal hall, with chandeliers and Eastern Ganga emblems
panels.action: Young Chandrika Devi sits in a carved wooden chair in a Ganga royal hall, listening as brahmins recite lineage, Eastern Ganga emblems and a lion standard visible behind her.

dialogue.text: The Kendupatna copper plates of Narasimhadeva II place Chandrika in the Eastern Ganga line—a princess tied by blood to Anangabhima III, the king who had bound Jagannatha to his crown.

i18n.hi: केन्दुपटना की नरसिंहदेव द्वितीय की ताम्रपट्टों में चन्द्रिका को पूर्वी गंगा वंश में रखा गया है—प्राण से अनंगभीम तृतीय की बेटी, उस राजा की जो जगन्नाथ को अपने मुकुट से बाँध चुका था।

panels.shot: medium shot of Chandrika in a royal audience chamber as envoys arrive with banners
panels.action: Chandrika Devi stands beside the throne dais, watching Kalachuri envoys in distinctive dress present alliance proposals before the Eastern Ganga court.

dialogue.text: In that age, daughters were also diplomatic bridges. Chandrika was given in marriage to Paramardideva, a Haihaya-Kalachuri prince, sealing alliance between coastal Kalinga and the Narmada hinterland.

i18n.hi: उस दौर में बेटियाँ भी कूटनीतिक सेतु थीं। चन्द्रिका का विवाह हैहय-कलचुरी राजकुमार परमर्दिदेव से हुआ, जिससे तटीय कलिंग और नर्मदा के पिछवाड़े में संधि पक्की हुई।

panels.shot: wide shot of a ceremonial marriage pavilion, with two thrones and ritual fire
panels.action: A royal marriage pavilion glows with firelight as Chandrika Devi and Paramardideva sit side by side before the sacred fire, surrounded by priests, courtiers, and ornaments of both Ganga and Kalachuri styles.

dialogue.speaker: chandrika_devi
dialogue.text: From my father’s river to his… may duty bridge these worlds.

i18n.hi: मेरे पिता की नदी से उसकी नदी तक… कर्तव्य इन दुनियाओं को जोड़े।

panels.shot: dynamic wide of cavalry and war-elephants moving across a flat Bengal landscape
panels.action: Kalachuri and allied forces ride and march across a misty Bengal plain, pennons flying, elephants caparisoned, the sky heavy with monsoon clouds.

dialogue.text: The eastern frontier was restless. As the Ganga kings pushed into Bengal, tradition recalls Paramardideva riding to that theatre. Somewhere in those campaigns, the princess’s husband vanished from the record.

i18n.hi: पूरब की सीमा अशांत थी। गंगा राजा बंगाल की ओर बढ़ रहे थे, परंपरा कहती है परमर्दिदेव उसी युद्धभूमि की ओर सवार हुआ। उन अभियानों की कहीं एक जगह, राजकुमारी का पति लेखों से गायब हो गया।

panels.shot: close-up on Chandrika’s face in a quiet palace chamber, with a letter sealed beside her
panels.action: Chandrika Devi sits alone in a dim chamber, a folded letter with broken seal on a low table, her gaze fixed and distant, lamps burning low.

dialogue.text: There is no chronicler’s description of that moment. Only the later inscription hints at a widow’s status. But it is clear: Paramardideva died, and Chandrika returned to Odisha with grief and the assets of a royal woman.

i18n.hi: उस पल का कोई इतिहासकार वर्णन नहीं करता। बस बाद का शिलालेख एक विधवा की स्थिति की ओर इशारा करता है। पर बात साफ है: परमर्दिदेव मरा, और चन्द्रिका शोक और राजसी संपदा के साथ ओडिशा लौट आई।

panels.shot: high-angle interior of a Bhubaneswar royal residence overlooking temple spires
panels.action: From a balcony, Chandrika Devi looks out over Bhubaneswar’s Shaiva temples, their towers rising beyond trees, while a brahmin adviser holds scrolls describing local shrines.

dialogue.text: Back in Bhubaneswar, she saw the stone forest of Shiva’s shrines. Lingas filled the precincts; Vaishnava images were scattered here and there, but no great Vishnu temple anchored the city’s heart.

i18n.hi: भुवनेश्वर लौटकर उसने शिव के पत्थर-जंगल को देखा। लिंगों से चौहद्दी भरी थी; वैष्णव मूर्तियाँ इधर-उधर बिखरी थीं, पर कोई महान विष्णु मंदिर शहर के दिल में जड़ नहीं था।

panels.shot: medium shot in a consultation scene, with Chandrika before architects and sthapatis
panels.action: Chandrika Devi sits upright on a cushioned seat, facing temple architects and sthapatis who unroll palm-leaf designs and draw plans for a proposed Vishnu temple.

dialogue.text: It was here that Chandrika moved from royal mourner to patron. The Ananta Vasudeva inscription states that she caused the temple to be built—a rare female name carved into Odisha’s monumental stone.

i18n.hi: यहीं चन्द्रिका राजदरबार की शोकमग्न से संरक्षक बनी। अनन्त वासुदेव की अभिलेख साफ लिखती है कि मंदिर उसी ने बनवाया—ओडिशा की विशाल शिल्प-धरा पर उकेरा गया एक दुर्लभ स्त्री नाम।

panels.shot: low-angle shot of Chandrika examining carved stone blocks with Vaishnava motifs at a construction yard
panels.action: In a bustling stone yard, Chandrika Devi walks among sculpted blocks bearing Shankha, Chakra, Garuda, and serpent motifs, while craftsmen chip away at fresh khondalite stone.

dialogue.speaker: chandrika_devi
dialogue.text: Bhubaneswar must also know the form of the Blue Lord. Let us raise his house.

i18n.hi: भुवनेश्वर भी नीले प्रभु की आकृति जाने। आओ, उसका घर उठाएँ।

panels.shot: wide construction scene with scaffolding around the rising temple tower near Bindusagar
panels.action: Scaffolding of bamboo and wood wraps around the rising Ananta Vasudeva tower, labourers hauling stone, sculptors working on niches, with the waters of Bindusagar tank gleaming beyond.

dialogue.text: Panel by panel, the structure rose beside Bindusagar. Its plan echoed the Lingaraja temple’s form, yet the imagery and dedication turned toward Vishnu as Ananta Vasudeva, the serpent-borne Lord.

i18n.hi: पैनल दर पैनल, ढाँचा बिन्दुसागर के किनारे उठता गया। योजना लिंगराज मंदिर की छवि दोहराती थी, पर प्रतिमाएँ और समर्पण विष्णु-अनन्त वासुदेव, शेषनाग-शायी प्रभु, की ओर मुड़ गए।

panels.shot: close-up on a sculpted Vishnu image being hoisted, Chandrika watching from below
panels.action: A large stone image of Vishnu in standing pose is being lifted by ropes toward the sanctum, while Chandrika Devi stands below, hands folded in reverence.

dialogue.text: Donaldson and others read its art as clearly Vaishnava—Vishnu with Shankha and Chakra, flanked by his attendants—set within a city otherwise dominated by Shaiva iconography.

i18n.hi: डोनाल्डसन और अन्य इसे साफ वैष्णव कला मानते हैं—शंख और चक्र वाले विष्णु, सेवकों से घिरे—एक ऐसे शहर के भीतर, जो बाकी जगह शिव प्रतिमाओं से भरा था।

panels.shot: interior sanctum mid-shot with lamp-lit deity and Chandrika offering flowers
panels.action: Inside the dark sanctum, lit by a single oil lamp, the installed Ananta Vasudeva image stands on the pedestal as Chandrika Devi gently places a garland at the deity’s feet.

dialogue.text: When consecration came, priests recited mantras and lit lamps. The inscription credits Chandrika as the one who endowed this house, marking a woman’s agency at the core of a royal religious project.

i18n.hi: जब प्राण प्रतिष्ठा आयी, पुजारी मंत्र पढ़ने लगे और दीप जले। अभिलेख इस घर की दानी चन्द्रिका को मानता है—राजसी धार्मिक परियोजना के केंद्र में एक स्त्री की पहल दर्ज होती है।

panels.shot: processional wide shot outside the completed temple, with devotees and brahmins
panels.action: A festival-like scene shows devotees, brahmins, and musicians gathered before the completed Ananta Vasudeva temple, its fresh carvings bright, as Chandrika Devi watches calmly from the side.

dialogue.text: Her act did not overturn the city’s Shaiva character. Lingaraja’s grand compound still dominated. But the presence of Ananta Vasudeva declared that royal patronage now also flowed toward Vishnu in Bhubaneswar itself.

i18n.hi: उसके कार्य ने शहर के शैव स्वभाव को नहीं पलटा। लिंगराज का विराट प्रांगण अब भी हावी था। पर अनन्त वासुदेव की मौजूदगी ने ऐलान किया कि राजसी संरक्षण अब भुवनेश्वर में विष्णु की ओर भी बह रहा है।

panels.shot: comparative wide shot juxtaposing Ananta Vasudeva’s tower with a hint of Konarak’s Sun Temple silhouette in the distance
panels.action: The Ananta Vasudeva temple stands near Bindusagar, while in the far coastal distance, the faint silhouette of Konarak’s great Sun Temple rises on the horizon under a blazing sky.

dialogue.text: Debala Mitra and Donaldson place her work within a larger pattern. In the same century, kings like Narasimhadeva I raised Konarak’s vast Sun Temple. Chandrika’s shrine was a quieter, but still monumental, shift in religious landscape.

i18n.hi: देबला मित्रा और डोनाल्डसन उसके काम को एक बड़े पैटर्न में रखते हैं। उसी सदी में नरसिंहदेव प्रथम जैसे राजा कोणार्क का विराट सूर्य मंदिर उठाते हैं। चन्द्रिका का मंदिर शांत, पर फिर भी धार्मिक भूगोल में एक महत्त्वपूर्ण, पत्थर का मोड़ था।

panels.shot: time-lapse style wide shot of the temple across ages, with subtle changes in masonry hinting at Maratha renovations
panels.action: The Ananta Vasudeva temple is shown in three ghosted overlays—original medieval stone, additional upper masonry and altered entrance features—suggesting later modifications over time.

dialogue.text: Later Maratha patrons would renovate and alter parts of the temple. The structure we see today is layered history. Yet beneath those additions, the core plan and dedication trace back to Chandrika’s 13th-century commission.

i18n.hi: बाद के मराठा संरक्षकों ने मंदिर के हिस्सों को सुधारा और बदल दिया। आज जो संरचना दिखती है, वो तहों वाली इतिहास है। पर इन परतों के नीचे, मूल योजना और समर्पण सीधा चन्द्रिका के तेरहवीं सदी के आदेश तक जाता है।

panels.shot: extreme close-up on Chandrika’s aged profile in soft light, overlaid with faint script of the inscription
panels.action: An older Chandrika Devi’s profile is seen in soft light, thoughtful, while translucent Odia script from the Ananta Vasudeva inscription hovers beside her like a memory.

dialogue.text: We do not know where she died, or what words she left behind. What we do know is what the inscription chose to fix: her name, her lineage, and the fact that she built this Vishnu temple in Shaiva Bhubaneswar.

i18n.hi: हम नहीं जानते वह कहाँ मरी, या कौन से शब्द पीछे छोड़ गई। जो हम जानते हैं, वो है जो अभिलेख ने बाँधकर रखा: उसका नाम, उसका वंश, और यह तथ्य कि उसने शैव भुवनेश्वर में यह विष्णु मंदिर बनवाया।

panels.shot: sweeping crane shot pulling up from Chandrika before the temple into the sky, revealing the city
panels.action: Chandrika Devi stands small but steady before the Ananta Vasudeva temple as the camera pulls up, the temple aligning with Lingaraja and other spires in the wider cityscape.

dialogue.text: Chandrika Devi’s story reminds us that in medieval India, stone did not speak only of kings. When a widowed princess chose to act, her decision reshaped a sacred city—and carved a woman’s will into its skyline forever.

i18n.hi: चन्द्रिका देवी की कहानी दिखाती है कि मध्ययुगीन भारत में पत्थर सिर्फ राजाओं की आवाज़ नहीं था। जब एक विधवा राजकुमारी ने कदम उठाने का चुना, उसके निर्णय ने एक पवित्र शहर को बदला—और उसके इरादे को उसकी रेखाओं में हमेशा के लिए तराश दिया।

title_i18n.en: Chandrika Devi Builds the Blue God's House
title_i18n.hi: चन्द्रिका देवी ने नीले देवता का घर उठाया
